support_spans: 4-hour history of acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
perforated appendix with a 51×31×26 mm collection and surrounding fat stranding
concepts.why: The patient presented with acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain and was found to have a perforated appendix with surrounding fat stranding.

support_spans: bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy contiguous with soft tissue thickening enveloping the right lower and middle lobe bronchi
concepts.why: The patient had innumerable hepatic nodules and bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy, suggesting metastatic disease, and a thickened sigmoid colon was found during exploratory laparotomy.
The patient presented with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, indicating a systemic inflammatory response.

support_spans: bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy contiguous with soft tissue thickening enveloping the right lower and middle lobe bronchi
concepts.why: The patient had a history of prostate cancer and presented with findings suggestive of metastatic disease, including innumerable hepatic nodules and bulky lymphadenopathy.

support_spans: pulmonary consolidation and collapse in the right lower lobe
concepts.why: The patient had pulmonary consolidation and collapse in the right lower lobe, suggesting a pulmonary infection.

rationales.F06: Acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain is a classic symptom of appendicitis.
rationales.F10: A perforated appendix is a definitive diagnosis of appendicitis.
rationales.F11: Innumerable hepatic nodules could indicate metastatic disease, including metastatic prostate cancer.
rationales.F12: Bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy and soft tissue thickening enveloping the bronchi could indicate metastatic disease or pneumonia.

frontier_selector.why: The patient's presentation with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, along with the findings of peritonism and purulent contamination, most strongly supports sepsis as the primary diagnosis.
